subject: Unit economics deep-dive: next steps & pricing targets
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jasper Li <jasper@fintechx.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 16:10:00 +0000
Subject: Unit economics deep-dive: next steps & pricing targets

Thanks for the productive call today — great to meet the FintechX team. Quick recap and proposed next steps below.

1) Call summary
- Use case: customer support automation + risk-scoring enrichment for loan applications.
- Target features: conversational agent (web + mobile), automated triage, and realtime KV-enriched scoring.
- Current expected traffic: 5M–10M requests/month; avg payload ~1k tokens/request (prompt+response) initially, trending down as we tighten prompts.

2) Cost & pricing items we agreed to validate
- Monthly token volume bucket: 150M–1B tokens/month (we used your 5M–10M requests * 1k tokens as baseline).
- Target budget range: $25k–$80k/month (you mentioned mid-market pilot budget).
- Unit economics ask: target $/1M tokens threshold and margin targets vs inference cost (your finance wants to hit ~40–50% gross margin at feature level).
- CAC/payback expectation: you asked for guidance on expected payback window for the pilot vs expansion.

3) Proposed Redwood baseline & options (high-level)
- Baseline list pricing: $600 per 1M tokens (hosted API), with committed pricing and blended discounts available for committed Dedicated capacity.
- Suggested target for FintechX pilot: $400–500 per 1M tokens with a 6–12 month ramp and performance SLOs.
- Optional: quantization/engineered kernels on Dedicated to reduce inference cost by ~25–40% at scale — we can model exact $/1M for Dedicated after we get a sample workload.

4) Unit economics framing (for upcoming deep-dive)
- $/feature: we’ll model incremental inference cost per distinct feature (e.g., conversation session, risk-score enrichment) and tie to expected revenue per feature.
- CAC payback: show ARR uplift assumptions and compute months-to-payback given pilot conversion and expansion rates.
- Margin targets: map gross margin vs inference cost at multiple price points ($/1M) and identify break-evens.

5) Next steps / asks (action items)
- Jasper: confirm expected monthly token volume range (low/expected/high) and representative sample prompts (anonymized) so we can run a micro-benchmark.
- FintechX Finance: share target gross margin and any hard upper bound for $/1M tokens.
- Redwood: we’ll produce a 2–page unit-econ sketch + a sample pricing grid and propose a deep-dive call the week of Oct 5.

Attachments: unit-econ-deck.pdf (summary), sample-pricing-sheet.xlsx (pricing grid stub).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a proposed calendar invite once we get your volume confirmation.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0182

--
Redwood Inference — High-performance inference for production LLMs
From: Jasper Li <jasper@fintechx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: FintechX Finance <finance@fintechx.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 09:02:45 +0000
Subject: Re: Unit economics deep-dive: next steps & pricing targets

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. Quick answers from our side:

- Volume: pilot month 1 estimate ~160M tokens (5M requests * ~32 tokens effective after prompt trimming), ramp to ~600M tokens over 6 months if pilot converts. Long-term target 1B tokens+/month.
- Budget: pilot allocated $30k for month 1, stretch to $60k/month in ramp months; expansion budgeting TBD.
- Margin target: Finance is targeting ~45% gross margin at the feature/product level (post-inference cost).
- CAC/payback: as a rule we need SaaS payback under 12 months for pilots; 6–9 months preferred for strategic buys.

Requests:
- Can you provide a modeled sheet showing $/feature for (a) conversational sessions, (b) risk-score enrichment (per credit application), and (c) batched bulk enrichment? We can share sample volumes per feature.
- Can Redwood provide a ballpark $/1M tokens on Dedicated vs Hosted for 600M and 1B tiers (committed)?

If you can send an initial sketch by EOD Friday, we’ll route to Finance and try to get the sample prompts earlier this week.

Cheers,
Jasper Li
Head of Partnerships | FintechX
jasper@fintechx.com

Subject: Re: Unit economics deep-dive: next steps & pricing targets

Thanks Jasper — appreciate the clarity. Quick initial model and proposed next meeting.

Attached is a one-page sketch (also pasted below) — assumes average token consumption per feature using your pilot estimates. This is a high-level working model (we'll refine with sample prompts & perf data).

High-level suggested price bands (hosted API, committed pilot discounts applied):
- 150M–300M tokens/month: $650 per 1M tokens
- 300M–700M tokens/month: $500 per 1M tokens
- 700M–1B+ tokens/month: $350–420 per 1M tokens (aggressive committed pricing/Dedicated advisory)

Example $/feature (inference cost only, hosted list -> effective after volume discount):
- Conversational session (avg 1k tokens/session end-to-end): 1k tokens = 1.0 units -> at $500/1M = $0.50 per session inference cost.
- Risk-score enrichment (avg 200 tokens/call, per application): 0.2 units -> $0.10 per enrichment.
- Batched bulk enrichment (per 1k records batch, avg 50 tokens/record): 50k tokens -> $25 per batch inference cost.

Mapping to your margin target (45%):
- If you price the conversational feature at $1.25/session and inference cost is $0.50, gross margin ~60% before other infra/ops costs — comfortably above 45%.
- For enrichment priced at $0.35 per application with inference cost $0.10, margin ~71%.

CAC/payback assumptions (pilot -> expansion)
- If average contract value from pilot to expansion lifts ARR by $120k/yr and CAC on pilot is $30k (sales + implementation), payback ~3 months.
- We’ll include sensitivity rows for lower conversion / longer sales cycles to show 6–12 month payback scenarios.

Next steps:
- Please share 1) anonymized sample prompts for each feature and 2) expected monthly split by feature.
- Proposed deep-dive: Tue, Oct 6 at 10:00 PT — 45 minutes to review model + Dedicated economics. Rishi and Monica will join to answer perf/infra questions.

I’ll attach the one-pager and a sample pricing grid (csv/xlsx) — if this looks directionally right we’ll prepare a Dedicated cost model after we get sample traces.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments referenced: unit-econ-deck.pdf, sample-pricing-sheet.xlsx
